name: Helius
description: Dominant Solana RPC, indexing, and data infrastructure provider. Offers enhanced transaction APIs, DAS (Digital Asset Standard) API for NFTs/tokens, webhook streaming for real-time onchain events, and high-reliability RPC endpoints.

ecosystem_fit.notes: The default indexing and RPC choice for production Solana applications. Appears in the majority of production Solana repos.

common_pairings.context: Helius for data indexing and event triggers, Jito for execution. The canonical Solana trading agent data+execution stack.
Helius for onchain data, Turnkey for server-side wallet signing in autonomous agent stacks.
Helius for transaction data and event webhooks; Birdeye for market data (price, OHLCV, P&L). Used together in trading agents that need both data types.

trust_evidence.description: Helius appears in the majority of production Solana repositories as the primary RPC and indexing provider. Cited in Solana Foundation official resources.
Helius + Jito is the most frequently observed Solana trading agent pattern in the corpus. The pairing recurs across unrelated community skills (sendaifun, QuickNode).
Helius maintains a dedicated skill in the sendaifun community hub, indicating strong developer tooling investment.

scale_guidance.hackathon: Public Helius API key is sufficient. Use free tier.
scale_guidance.mvp: Upgrade to paid tier — rate limits on free tier will cause failures under any real load.
scale_guidance.production: Plan Helius rate limit tier before launch. Webhook reliability is critical for event-driven agents — test failure modes.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: When multi-chain RPC support is needed (not Solana-only). QuickNode also supports Solana but Helius is the Solana-native choice.

anti_patterns: Using public Solana RPCs instead of Helius at production scale — public RPCs have strict rate limits that will fail under agent workloads.
Using Helius for Ethereum or Base data — Helius is Solana-only. Use Alchemy or QuickNode for EVM chains.
Not planning for Helius webhook reliability in production — agents that depend on webhooks for triggers need retry logic.
